description: Sync the messages a Discord bot can read in the servers you choose, one document per message. Discord channel and role permissions are not carried over.
opening: Sync messages from the Discord servers you select: channel histories, including the text chat of voice and stage channels, and active and archived threads, including forum and media threads. Each message is one document. A reply is its own document and links to the message it answers. Text from PDF and DOCX attachments is searchable with the message when it can be read.

Discord permissions are not imported, so private and role-restricted channels are visible to everyone who can query the collection unless you set an access rule on the server. Each sync reads the server's lookback window again, so edits inside it are picked up. Messages deleted in Discord stay in HydraDB.

notes: Discord does not expose member email addresses, so roles and channel permissions cannot be matched to the people who query HydraDB.
Private channels and role-restricted channels are not restricted in HydraDB. Set an access rule on the server if they must stay private.

connect.auth: Discord uses the token of a bot in your Discord application. What the bot can read comes from the permissions it is granted when you invite it.

credentials.name: bot_token
credentials.text: The token of a bot in your Discord application.

permissions.name: bot
permissions.text: OAuth2 scope, used when you invite the bot.

permissions.name: Message Content Intent
permissions.text: turned on under Bot, Privileged Gateway Intents.

connect.permissions_note: Without Message Content Intent, every sync fails rather than indexing empty messages.

steps.title: Create a bot
steps.text: In the Discord Developer Portal, create an application and a bot, and copy the bot token.

steps.title: Turn on Message Content Intent
steps.text: Under Bot, Privileged Gateway Intents, turn on Message Content Intent. HydraDB checks it and refuses to sync without it.

steps.title: Invite the bot
steps.text: Invite the bot to each server with the OAuth2 scope `bot`. Grant View Channels and Read Message History on every channel to sync.

steps.title: Select servers
steps.text: HydraDB lists every server the bot is a member of. Select the servers to sync. With no server selected, nothing is synced.

connect.account: One connector reads the servers one Discord bot has joined.

sync.first_sync: Each server reaches back the window set by `lookback_days`, 30 days by default.
sync.changes: Each sync reads the server's lookback window again and updates messages by id.
sync.edits: An edit is picked up while the message is still inside the server's lookback window. Edits to older messages are not.
sync.deletes: Deleted messages are not removed. A message deleted in Discord stays searchable in HydraDB.
notes: A private archived thread is read only when the bot can see it or has joined it. Histories the bot cannot read are skipped with a warning.

Through the API, you can choose to sync only new messages: set `sync_mode` to `new_only` on a server when you configure the connector. Edits to older messages are then missed, even inside the lookback window.

shared_attributes.name: author
shared_attributes.text: The author's server nickname, else global display name, else username. On a message it is the From line, and the graph records the message as sent by that person. On a reply it is the Author line, and the graph records the reply as written by that person.

shared_attributes.name: created_at
shared_attributes.text: When the message was sent, written as the Sent line on a message and the Created line on a reply.

shared_attributes.name: updated_at
shared_attributes.text: When the message was last edited, else when it was sent. Searchable on replies, as the Updated line. Not searchable on other messages.

shared_attributes.name: mentions
shared_attributes.text: Display names of the users mentioned. Known mentions are written into the text as names. The graph records each as mentioned. A mention that cannot be resolved keeps its raw Discord syntax.

shared_attributes.name: attachments
shared_attributes.text: Attachment file names, written after `Attachments:`. A message whose only content is a file of an unsupported type is still found by its file name.

shared_attributes.name: Attachment text
shared_attributes.text: Text read from PDF and DOCX attachments, searchable with the message.

shared_attributes.name: stickers
shared_attributes.text: Sticker names, written after `Stickers:`.

shared_attributes.name: Reply or forward reference
shared_attributes.text: The message this one replies to or forwards. Joins a reply to the message it answers, and a forward to its original. Not searchable as a link, though a reply's text ends with the parent message id.

shared_attributes.name: Loom links
shared_attributes.text: Loom share or embed links in the text or in embeds, up to 50 per message. Links the message to that Loom video. Not searchable as a link, though the link stays in the text.

shared_attributes.name: additional_metadata.discord_message_id
shared_attributes.text: The message id. Picks out one message. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: additional_metadata.discord_server_id
shared_attributes.text: The server id. Limits a query to one server. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: additional_metadata.discord_channel_id
shared_attributes.text: The channel or thread id. Limits a query to one channel or thread. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: additional_metadata.discord_author_id
shared_attributes.text: The author's user or bot id. Limits a query to one author, even after a display name change. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: additional_metadata.discord_message_type
shared_attributes.text: Discord's numeric message type. Includes or excludes message types. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: additional_metadata.pinned
shared_attributes.text: Whether the message was pinned when it was synced. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: additional_metadata.tts
shared_attributes.text: Whether the message was sent as text-to-speech. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: additional_metadata.has_attachments
shared_attributes.text: Whether the message has at least one named attachment, even when the file text could not be read. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: additional_metadata.rbac_warning
shared_attributes.text: A fixed note on every message that Discord permissions are not imported. An access rule you set on the server still applies. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: connector_id
shared_attributes.text: Limits a query to this connector's messages. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: provider
shared_attributes.text: Always `discord`. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: channel
shared_attributes.text: The channel or thread name, so you can see where a result came from. To limit a query to a channel, use `additional_metadata.discord_channel_id`.

shared_attributes.name: server
shared_attributes.text: The server name. To limit a query to a server, use `additional_metadata.discord_server_id`.

shared_attributes.name: is_edited
shared_attributes.text: Whether Discord reports the message as edited.

shared_attributes.name: edited_at
shared_attributes.text: When Discord reports the message was last edited, empty if never.

documents.name: Messages
documents.one_document: One Discord message that is not a reply. A forwarded message is a message too.
documents.title: `#channel` and the author's display name. Search matches the message text, not this title, so a channel name in a query does not limit results to that channel.
documents.text: The message text, with user, role and channel mentions turned into names and custom emoji shown as `:name:`. Then embed titles, descriptions and fields, the poll question and answers, interactive component text and forwarded message text. Then `Attachments:` with file names and `Stickers:` with sticker names. The author is written as a From line and the time as a Sent line. A message with none of these is skipped.
documents.date: When the message was last edited, else when it was sent.
documents.link_back: A discord.com link to the message, when the server and channel ids are known.
documents.files: PDF and DOCX attachments up to 20 MiB are downloaded and read, and their text is searchable with the message. If reading fails, the message is still kept. Other files contribute only their names.

attributes.name: Server
attributes.text: The selected server. An access rule you set on it governs its messages. Not searchable.

documents.name: Replies
documents.one_document: One message that replies to another message.
documents.title: `#channel` and the author's display name. Search matches the reply text, not this title.
documents.text: Built like a message's text, ending with `Reply to message:` and the parent message id. The author is written as an Author line, with Created and Updated lines.
documents.date: When the reply was last edited, else when it was sent.
documents.link_back: A discord.com link to the reply, when the server and channel ids are known.
documents.files: As for messages: PDF and DOCX attachments up to 20 MiB are read, and other files contribute only their names.

attributes.name: Server
attributes.text: The selected server. An access rule you set on it governs its replies. Not searchable.

example_searches: What did the community say about the release, limited to the announcements channel's id?
Who replied to the bug report, and what did they suggest?
What does the setup guide PDF posted in Discord say about configuring the bot?

connections: A reply to the message it answers.
A forwarded message to its original.
A message to any Loom video it links to, which resolves when that video is synced into the same collection.
Channels and servers are kept as labels, not linked.
No other links to other tools.
people: The author of each message or reply.
Users mentioned in a message, by display name.
The author's id is a query filter, not a person in the graph.
graph.from_text: The message text, embed text and text read from attachments.

not_synced: Servers you did not select, and channels and private threads the bot cannot read.
Voice and stage audio and video.
Forum and media parent objects, apart from the messages in their threads.
Attachment contents other than PDF and DOCX, files over 20 MiB, and files that cannot be read.
Deletions: deleted messages stay in HydraDB.
Member email addresses and Discord permissions. Role names are used only to turn mentions into names.
